A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NECS should be considered a neuroectodermal neoplasm, which is probably a primitive tumor of neuroendocrine cells of the skin.
the diagnosis of NECS is based on a careful analysis of morphological, immunohistochemical and ultrastructural features.

the immunophenotype of NECS consists in the co-expression of intermediate filaments (cytokeratins and/or neurofilaments) and of the absence of CLA, S-100 protein, vimentin and other neuroendocrine markers (except for chromogranin A).

immunophenotyping is an indispensable tool for a more exact and differential diagnosis of NECS.
immunohistochemical studies of NECS are essential for an exact diagnosis and for a more appropriate treatment.
